$comment: THE ONE RULE TABLE FOR WHICH ROUTE DOES WHICH WORK (owner, 13 Nov 2026). Read by src/shared/ai/seatOrder.ts (the Worker's router) and scripts/lib/model-roles.mjs (the Mac's job runner); nothing else holds an order. It speaks of job class, route tier (the free lanes, the Codex seat, the Claude Code seat) and the privacy limit, never of a model's name. A concrete model id may appear only under seat_invocation: it is what a seat is started with, not a rule about any job.

classes.$comment: Job class by ability, and the row each takes when the work is private or not. HARD = hard judgement and long builds: writes code that lands, decides, merges, reviews, repairs, touches money, edits the Fund deck, or writes what a partner or outsider reads unchecked. CLEAR_BRIEF = well-specified work with a clear brief: housekeeping, docs, bulk edits. SHORT = short and checkable: sorting mail, summaries, first drafts, routine searches, read-only lists that something else checks. A class nobody named is HARD.

order.$comment: seats: the subscription seats a row may use, in order; a seat not listed takes no part. free: where the free (training-permitting) lanes stand. freeLanes: the free lanes in today's order; the router re-ranks them per duty kind from the ai_run log (the lane that last completed the kind first, a lane that failed it twice running left out for a day). PRIVATE rows never have a free lane: that is a limit on a route's data use, not on ability, and no other marker can lift it. PRIVATE_HARD waits for Claude Code by name and never goes to Codex.

seat_invocation.$comment: What each seat's CLI is started with for a local job. Data for the seat, not a rule about a job: change it here and every job follows.
